newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE cigarettes must cut tar, nicotine by November.
newsitem.headline: UAE cigarettes must cut tar, nicotine by November.

text.p: Cigarette companies in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have been given three months' grace from August 26 to reduce nicotine and tar levels in cigarettes to 0.6 mg and 10 mg respectively, newspapers said on Monday.
The grace period was announced by the UAE municipalities general secretariat on Sunday, daily Khaleej Times said.
The cut in nicotine and tar levels is in line with Gulf-wide regulations agreed by the Gulf Cooperation Council, which groups the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain and Qatar.
In a bid to curb smoking, Gulf Arab states have agreed to a gradual rise in cigarette duties to 100 percent.
